citeAs: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao (2024). Are We on the Right Way for Evaluating Large Vision-Language Models? arXiv:2403.20330.
creator: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao (University of Science and Technology of China; The Chinese University of Hong Kong; Shanghai AI Laboratory)
description: MMStar is an elite vision-indispensable multi-modal benchmark comprising 1,500 samples meticulously selected by humans. It benchmarks 6 core capabilities (Coarse Perception, Fine-grained Perception, Instance Reasoning, Logical Reasoning, Science & Technology, Mathematics) and 18 detailed axes, aiming to evaluate large vision-language models' multi-modal capacities with carefully balanced and purified samples that exhibit visual dependency, minimal data leakage, and require advanced multi-modal capabilities.
name: MMStar
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each sample was reviewed by three human experts during the manual review phase.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Three domain experts conducted the manual review. No further demographic details (nationality, age, gender) are provided in the paper.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three human experts conducted manual review of the coarsely filtered 11,607 samples to ensure: (1) each sample's answer is based on understanding visual content; (2) selected samples cover a comprehensive range of capability assessment dimensions; (3) most samples require LVLMs to possess advanced multi-modal abilities. Samples were split into four difficulty categories based on LVLM hit counts (easy, moderate, hard, tough), and 1,500 high-quality samples were manually curated considering both diversity of capability dimensions and difficulty levels.
rai:dataBiases: The paper explicitly identifies and addresses two biases in existing benchmarks that MMStar is designed to mitigate: (1) Visual content is unnecessary for many samples in existing benchmarks — answers can be inferred from text alone or world knowledge embedded in LLMs. (2) Unintentional data leakage exists in LLM and LVLM training, where models can answer visual-necessary questions without visual input by recalling training data. MMStar's curation process specifically filters for these issues. The paper also notes that the source benchmark composition is skewed toward SEED (63.5% of initial pool, 69% after coarse filter, 28.3% in final selection).
rai:dataCollection: Samples were first roughly selected from six existing benchmarks (SEED, AI2D, ScienceQA, MMBench, MathVista, MMMU) using an automated pipeline. Two closed-source LLMs (GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro) and six open-source LLMs (sizing 20B or larger, including LLaMA-70B, Qwen-1.5-72B, Mixtral-8x7B, etc.) served as inspectors to filter out samples answerable without visual input. Samples with hit counts of two or fewer (i.e., around 75% of LLM inspectors fail) were retained, reducing the pool from 22,401 to 11,607 candidate samples. Three human experts then conducted manual review to select 1,500 final high-quality samples.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Samples sourced from six existing multi-modal benchmarks: SEED-Image, AI2D-Test, ScienceQA-Test, MMBench-EN-Dev, MathVista-Mini, and MMMU-Val. The initial pool comprised 22,401 samples across these benchmarks.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataLimitations: The paper acknowledges that even with careful curation, some degree of data leakage may still exist (MMStar has the lowest average multi-modal leakage at 1.9 among benchmarks evaluated, but it is not zero). The benchmark is static with 1,500 samples, and the authors plan to expand it into a larger online test set in the future. The paper also notes that even the best model (GPT4V high-resolution) scores under 60% on average, suggesting the benchmark is challenging but also that evaluation may not yet be fully comprehensive.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: All questions were converted into a multiple-choice format. Samples were balanced across 6 core capability dimensions (250 samples each) and distributed relatively evenly across 18 detailed axes. Difficulty levels were assigned based on LVLM hit counts: easy (12-16 hits), moderate (8-11), hard (4-7), and tough (0-3).
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: An automated coarse filtering pipeline was applied: eight LLMs (two closed-source: GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro; six open-source: InternLM2-20B, Yi-34B, Mixtral-8x7B, Deepseek-67B, LLaMA2-70B, Qwen1.5-72B) evaluated each sample without visual input. Samples answerable by more than 2 of the 8 LLMs were excluded. Open-source LLMs used a 2-shot in-context inference strategy to minimize response refusals. This reduced the pool from 22,401 to 11,607 samples. Additionally, 16 leading LVLMs were used to gauge difficulty and split samples into four levels: easy (12-16 hits), moderate (8-11), hard (4-7), and tough (0-3).
rai:dataSocialImpact: MMStar aims to provide a more accurate and fair evaluation platform for LVLMs, addressing issues of visual dependency and data leakage that could lead to misjudgments of actual multi-modal capabilities and potentially misguide LVLM research. By ensuring evaluation samples genuinely require visual understanding, the benchmark helps the community better assess true multi-modal progress and avoid unfair model comparisons driven by data leakage.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating the multi-modal capabilities of large vision-language models (LVLMs), specifically ensuring visual dependency and minimal data leakage. The benchmark is intended to provide a fair and comprehensive arena for comparing LVLMs' actual multi-modal capacities across 6 core capability dimensions and 18 detailed axes.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Eight LLMs used as automated inspectors for coarse filtering: GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro (closed-source); InternLM2-20B, Yi-34B, Mixtral-8x7B, Deepseek-67B, LLaMA2-70B, Qwen1.5-72B (open-source). Additionally, 16 leading LVLMs (including GPT4V, GeminiPro-Vision, LLaVA series) were used to gauge sample difficulty and assign difficulty levels.
